Determine the largest interval on which the function $f(x)$ (shown above) is invertible.
feedback.worked_solution:
First, notice that the domain of our function is $x\in [-3,4).$

A function is invertible on a particular interval if and only if it's a one-to-one function on that interval. To determine the intervals on which the function is invertible, we use the horizontal line test.

- The function $f(x)$ does not pass the horizontal line test on the interval $x\in [1,4).$ In this case, the horizontal line $y=-1$ intersects the graph at more than one point.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture/13932058/assets/a709558673202ef4a7835dcea6e23b7ec5b13684272c56023058223c01fb8061.png)

- The function $f(x)$ is invertible on the interval $x\in [-3,1].$ On this interval, a horizontal line will intersect the curve at most once, no matter where we draw the line.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture/13932058/assets/5a65e71f571e9510580ba5fe105a6eac48acfe4564c5a6bf76371c2bf09ff651.png)

Therefore, the largest interval on which the function is invertible is:

$$
x\in [-3,1]
$$
